The village of Quintana, at the mouth of the Brazos River, was also destroyed.
In Victoria, Texas, the storm reached the city at about 7 AM, and an estimated 75 houses were destroyed.
In Victoria, Texas, another 118 houses were damaged; additionally, the town's jail, high school, freight station, Masonic hall, and certain sections were almost literally swept from the earth.
In Galveston, Texas, the storm damaged roads, railways, and houses, though no specific count of building damage was provided.

Time_Annotation: In late October, an active monsoon trough persisted south of Hawaii with an area of convection developing on October 24. Later that day the disturbance was classified as Tropical Depression Three-C, it became Tropical Storm Huko early on October 26, reached hurricane strength late on October 28, weakened to a tropical storm on October 30, re-attained hurricane strength on October 31, and on November 3 it crossed the International Date Line into the Western Pacific.
Administrative_Areas_Annotation: While passing near Johnston Atoll, the outer rainbands produced wind gusts up to 30 mph and locally heavy rainfall, and the remnants of Huko later reentered the basin, eventually affecting California.
Main_Event_Annotation: The system evolved from a Tropical Depression to Tropical Storm Huko and eventually reached hurricane strength before transitioning into a typhoon upon crossing the International Date Line, fitting the Tropical Storm/Cyclone category.
Hazards_Annotation: The outer rainbands generated wind gusts up to 30 mph and locally heavy rainfall which caused flooding along a small stream in Bakersfield.

Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Annotation: The tornado first struck Southaven High School, where 30 windows were broken, minor roof damage occurred, and damage was rated EF0.
In the nearby Carriage Hill subdivision, several homes sustained minor damage.

The tornado rapidly intensified to EF2 strength as it crossed the intersection of Stateline Road and Airways Boulevard, destroying three warehouse buildings. One of the buildings destroyed was the Cooper Lighting Plant.
A gas station in this area was damaged as well.

Considerable damage was reported at Memphis International Airport, where a hangar lost its roof, the FedEx freight terminal's fire station suffered roof damage, airstair trucks were thrown 100 yards, and aircraft were moved around.
In the Clarke Road area, tractor trailers were tossed around, a power substation was severely damaged, and several warehouse structures sustained heavy damage.
This included a DSC warehouse that was destroyed.
Numerous windows were shattered at the Willow Lake Business Park, and utility poles and trees were snapped in the area.
Multiple homes along Maple Tree Drive and Pinbranch Court were damaged, five of which sustained major damage.
The Hardy Bottling Company facility was also damaged.

Continuing northeast, the tornado weakened to EF1 strength and struck the Hickory Ridge Mall, resulting in total collapse of a large wall and much of the roof at the Sears department store. Damage surveyors noted very poor construction at this location, and six people in the mall were injured.
